# Amendment to Operating Agreement — Continuity Provisions (Template v2)

For a Florida LLC under ch. 605. Drafted for the single-member or owner-controlled company; multi-member variants in brackets. Statutory references confirmed against the 2026 Florida Statutes on 2026-11-01; v2 review 2026-11-08 (§§ 605.0105, 605.0106, 605.0107, 605.0302, 605.0401, 605.0407, 605.04071–605.04074, 605.0408, 605.0504, 605.0602, 605.0603, 605.0701 read that day).

**Why an amendment is required.** Under § 605.0602(7)(a) an individual member is dissociated on death, and the interest is then held only as a transferee's (§ 605.0603(1)(c)). The member's legal representative may exercise the member's rights, but only to settle the estate, including any power the member had to give a transferee the right to become a member (§ 605.0504). In a single-member company that leaves no member, and the company dissolves after 90 consecutive days without one unless a member is admitted (§ 605.0701(3)). Incapacity does *not* dissociate a member unless a guardian is appointed or a court so orders, and then only in a member-managed company (§ 605.0602(7)(b)); so an incapacitated sole member remains the only person with authority and cannot exercise it. A guardian of a member adjudged incompetent may exercise the member's rights to administer the member's property (§ 605.0504), which in a manager-managed company includes removing a manager without cause (§ 605.04072(4)). Neither default produces an authorized operator on day one, and either can remove one. The operating agreement may supply and protect one (§ 605.0105(1)), and this amendment does. A record filed with the Department prevails over the operating agreement as to third persons who reasonably rely on it (§ 605.0107(4)(b)), so the Sunbiz amendment and statement of authority in [ ].2(a) are part of the plan, not formalities.

---

AMENDMENT NO. [ ] TO THE OPERATING AGREEMENT OF [COMPANY], LLC

Effective [date], the Operating Agreement of [Company], LLC (the "Company") dated [ ] (the "Agreement") is amended by adding the following Article [ ] (Continuity). Capitalized terms not defined here have the meanings in the Agreement. If this Article conflicts with any other provision of the Agreement, this Article controls.

## Article [ ] — Continuity

### [ ].1 Definitions

(a) **"Principal"** means [Owner name], the [sole member / managing member / manager] of the Company.

(b) **"Unavailability Event"** means the first to occur of:

1. the Principal's death;
2. the Principal's **Incapacity**, meaning a written certification by [one / two] licensed physician[s][, one of whom is the Principal's attending physician, if any,] that the Principal is unable to manage the Company's affairs, whether or not a guardian has been appointed; or a court order to that effect; or
3. the Principal's **Unavailability**, meaning that the Principal has not communicated with the Company's bank, the Interim Manager, or the Company's counsel for [14] consecutive days and the Interim Manager, after reasonable attempts to reach the Principal, certifies in writing that the Principal is unavailable; or
4. the Principal's signed notice to the Interim Manager that the Principal elects to begin a Continuity Period.

(c) **"Interim Manager"** means [Name], or if [Name] is unable or unwilling to serve, [Alternate name], or if neither, the person designated under [ ].6.

(d) **"Continuity Period"** means the period beginning on an Unavailability Event and ending on the earliest of: (1) the Principal's written notice of return [with, in the case of Incapacity, a physician's certification of capacity]; (2) completion of a Branch Decision under [ ].5 and the actions it directs; or (3) [12] months, unless extended under [ ].5. If the period would end under clause (3) without a Branch Decision, the default branch in [ ].5 is the Branch Decision, and the Continuity Period continues until the actions it directs are complete.

(e) **"Cash Rule"** means the spending authority in Schedule 1.

(f) **"Cause"** means the Interim Manager's material breach of this Article or Schedule 1 not cured within [10] days after notice; conduct described in § 605.04091(3); conviction of, or plea of no contest to, a felony; or inability to serve for [30] consecutive days.

### [ ].2 Authority of the Interim Manager

(a) On an Unavailability Event, the Interim Manager becomes the sole manager of the Company for the Continuity Period, with the authority in this Article, without any further act, vote, or filing. Any authority of the Principal as a manager is suspended for the Continuity Period, and a matter for the managers is decided by the Interim Manager alone (varying § 605.04073(2)(b)). [If member-managed: *Effective on an Unavailability Event, the Company is a manager-managed limited liability company (§ 605.0407(1)(a)); it becomes member-managed again when a Continuity Period ends on the Principal's return.*] Within [10] days after the Unavailability Event, the Interim Manager shall sign and deliver to the Department for filing any amendment to the articles of organization or annual-report information needed to show the Interim Manager as manager, and a statement of authority under § 605.0302 stating the Interim Manager's authority under this Article; the Company shall amend or cancel the statement when the Continuity Period ends (§ 605.0302(2)). [Drafter: a filed record prevails as to third persons who rely on it (§ 605.0107(4)(b)). A statement of authority is conclusive for a person who gives value in reliance, other than on real-property transfers (§ 605.0302(5)), and lapses by law after 5 years (§ 605.0302(10)). Walk to the Department's current forms before first filing.]

(b) During the Continuity Period the Interim Manager has full authority to operate the Company in the ordinary course, including to: sign checks and electronic payments and act as signatory on all Company accounts; run payroll and hire, direct, and dismiss employees; collect receivables; pay creditors; perform, renew, and terminate contracts and leases in the ordinary course; deal with the Company's landlord, lenders, insurers, licensing agencies, and regulators; maintain and renew licenses and insurance; access all Company systems, credentials, and records; engage counsel, accountants, and other advisors; and take any other action a manager may take under ch. 605, subject only to the Cash Rule and [ ].3.

(c) The Interim Manager may not, without a Branch Decision under [ ].5: sell or encumber substantially all of the Company's assets; admit a member or issue interests; merge, convert, or dissolve the Company; make distributions other than tax distributions under Schedule 1; incur debt or personal guaranties outside the Cash Rule; or change the Company's line of business. Nothing in this Article varies a member's right to approve a merger, interest exchange, or conversion (§ 605.0105(3)(m)).

(c-1) Before any distribution, including a tax distribution, the Interim Manager shall determine in writing, on financial statements or a valuation method that is reasonable under the circumstances (§ 605.0405(2)), and may rely for that purpose on financial statements prepared or presented by the Company's [public accountant] (§ 605.04091(6)(b)), that the distribution is not prohibited by § 605.0405(1), and shall deliver the determination to the [Family Liaison] and counsel. [Drafter: § 605.0406(1) makes a consenting manager who fails § 605.04091 personally liable for the excess. The duty of care is breached by "grossly negligent or reckless conduct, willful or intentional misconduct, or a knowing violation of law" (§ 605.04091(3)); reliance on an accountant's statements is protected unless the manager knows facts that make it unwarranted (§ 605.04091(6)–(7)). This clause documents the reliance.]

(d) The Interim Manager owes the duties of a manager under § 605.04091 and is indemnified to the fullest extent § 605.0408(2) permits, subject to § 605.0105(3)(p). The Company shall advance the Interim Manager's reasonable expenses, including attorney fees, of defending a claim arising from service, on the Interim Manager's signed promise to repay if not entitled to indemnification (§ 605.0408(3)), and [shall / may] maintain insurance for the Interim Manager's benefit (§ 605.0408(4)). The Interim Manager is entitled to compensation of [$ ] per [month] during the Continuity Period, payable from Company funds, set by reference to [the market rate for a comparable general manager, per the attached comparison]. [Drafter: the manager's pay is a manager's conflict of interest transaction (§ 605.04091(2)(b), § 605.04092(1)(e)). In a single-member company the burden-shifting approval of § 605.04092(4)(a) is unavailable: it "cannot be authorized, approved, or ratified … solely by a single member" or "solely by a single manager." The protection is fairness at the time of authorization (§ 605.04092(3)), meaning beneficial to the Company and comparable to an arm's length deal ((1)(c)); keep the comparison with this Article. If the Interim Manager is the Principal's spouse, child, parent, sibling or in-law, the Principal also has an indirect interest ((1)(b), (d)).] [If the Principal dies: a personal representative winding up the Company is subject to § 605.04091 (§ 605.04091(9)).]

(e) Third parties may rely conclusively on a written certificate of the Interim Manager, with the physician's certification or death certificate attached where applicable, that an Unavailability Event has occurred and that the Interim Manager is authorized to act. The Company shall deliver a copy of this Article and a form of certificate to each bank where it holds an account at signing.

(f) During a Continuity Period the Interim Manager may be removed only for Cause, by a signed record of [the Family Liaison with the consent of the person holding Branch Decision authority], and § 605.04072(4) does not apply. The successor is determined under [ ].1(c) and [ ].6. The Interim Manager may resign on [30] days' signed notice to the Family Liaison.

### [ ].3 Cash Rule
The Interim Manager shall operate within Schedule 1 (reserve account, authorized expenditures, limits, and reporting). Expenditures outside Schedule 1 require the written consent of the [Family Liaison / other members].

### [ ].4 Death; admission to avoid dissolution
On the Principal's death: (a) the Principal's interest passes under the Principal's estate plan and the transfer restrictions of the Agreement; (b) the Interim Manager's authority continues under this Article; and (c) [If single-member: the Company consents to admit as a member (§ 605.0401(3)(a)), effective on the Principal's death or, if later, on the person's signed acceptance of this Agreement, the trustee of [trust] if the Principal's interest passes to that trust, and otherwise the Principal's personal representative, so that the Company is not without a member for purposes of § 605.0701(3), pending transfer of the interest.] [Drafter: if the Principal holds the interest as trustee of a revocable trust, the member is the trustee, the trustee's death is not a § 605.0602(7) event, and a DPOA agent cannot act for the Principal as trustee (§ 709.2201(3)(e)). The successor-trustee provisions of the trust must then supply the member's authority; check them against this Article.] [Multi-member: the remaining members' rights under the Agreement and any buy-sell agreement are unaffected.]

### [ ].5 Branch Decision
No later than [30] days after an Unavailability Event, and again at [90] days if no decision has been made, the Interim Manager shall deliver to [the Family Liaison and the Company's counsel] a report of the Company's financial condition, pipeline, and staffing. The decision whether the Company will **continue**, be **sold**, or be **wound down** (the "Branch Decision") is made by [the Principal's attorney-in-fact under the Principal's durable power of attorney / the personal representative or trustee / the Interim Manager with the written consent of the Family Liaison]. The Company's default branch is **[continue / sell / wind down]**, which the Interim Manager shall prepare for unless a different Branch Decision is made. On a Branch Decision to sell or wind down, the Interim Manager has the additional authority in Schedule 2. Where ch. 605 or the Agreement requires a vote or consent of the members, it is given for the Principal's interest by the Principal's attorney-in-fact during the Principal's Incapacity or Unavailability, and after the Principal's death by the member admitted under [ ].4(c) or, until then, the Principal's legal representative (§ 605.0504).

### [ ].6 Family Liaison; successor Interim Manager
The **Family Liaison** is [Name], or if unable, [Alternate]. The Family Liaison receives the Interim Manager's reports, gives the consents this Article requires of the Family Liaison, and, if no Interim Manager named in [ ].1(c) is able to serve, designates one in writing [with the consent of the Principal's attorney-in-fact].

### [ ].7 Coordination with the Principal's personal documents
The Principal's durable power of attorney and estate-planning documents shall be consistent with this Article as to the identity of the Interim Manager, the Branch Decision authority, and the disposition of the Principal's interest. In the event of inconsistency, [this Article / the Principal's durable power of attorney] controls as to management of the Company, and the Principal's estate-planning documents control as to ownership of the interest.

### [ ].8 Review
The Company shall review this Article, Schedule 1, and Schedule 2 at least annually and on any change of Interim Manager, bank, lender, lease, or key employee.

### [ ].9 Amendment
This Article may be amended only in a writing signed by the Principal [and members holding ___%]. During a Continuity Period it may be amended only by the person holding Branch Decision authority with the signed approval of the Family Liaison, and an amendment adopted without that approval is ineffective (§ 605.0107(1)).

### [ ].10 General
This Article and any consent, certificate, or notice under it may be signed electronically and in counterparts (§ 605.0102 "sign"; § 668.50(7)). If a provision is held unenforceable, the rest of this Article continues in effect, and the provision is enforced to the extent permitted.

Except as amended here, the Agreement remains in full force.

[COMPANY], LLC
By: ______________________ [Principal], [Member/Manager]

**Approval of members (§ 605.04073(1)(d), (2)(e)):** The undersigned, being all the members of the Company, approve this Amendment.
______________________ [Principal], individually
[Multi-member: ______________________ [Member name]]

Their interests in this Article may differ from yours, including on your compensation, authority and indemnity. [Counsel] cannot give you legal advice about it, other than that you may want your own lawyer to review it before you sign. [Drafter: Rule 4-4.3(a). The comment allows Counsel to explain its own view of what the Article means once this is said.]

## Schedule 1 — Cash Rule
- Reserve account: [bank], target balance equal to [90] days of payroll and fixed costs ($[ ]).
- Authorized without consent: payroll and benefits; rent; insurance; taxes; utilities; vendors in the ordinary course up to $[ ] per vendor per month; professional fees up to $[ ].
- Requires Family Liaison consent: any single expenditure over $[ ]; any new debt; any capital purchase.
- Tax distributions: [formula], each subject to the written determination in [ ].2(c-1).
- Payments to the Principal during an Unavailability Event: only [under the Company's bona fide disability or benefits program / as reasonable compensation for past service], or as a distribution meeting [ ].2(c-1). [Drafter: § 605.0102(17)(b) excludes these two categories from "distribution"; anything else paid to the owner is a distribution tested under § 605.0405.]
- Reporting: monthly statement to the Family Liaison and counsel.

## Schedule 2 — Additional authority on a sell or wind-down Branch Decision
- **Sell:** engage a broker or valuator; negotiate and sign a letter of intent; sign a purchase agreement for the business or its assets [subject to approval of the person holding Branch Decision authority]; valuation reference: [method]; buyer list: [attached].
- **Wind down:** cease operations on a schedule; notify customers and referral sources; collect receivables; sell the customer list, equipment, and inventory; terminate the lease, licenses, insurance, and subscriptions; final payroll and employee notices; creditor claims; file articles of dissolution and wind up under §§ 605.0701–605.0713.

## Companion documents (not part of this amendment)
- Bank certificate form (for [ ].2(e)); signatory card update
- Durable power of attorney with business powers (ch. 709), naming the same Interim Manager as agent for the Principal's interest, or expressly deferring to this Article
- Instruction letter (contact tree, credentials, vendors)
- Physician certification form, and the Principal's signed authorization for each physician to release the certification (not the records) to the Interim Manager and Family Liaison [Drafter: HIPAA authorization, 45 C.F.R. § 164.508 — walk to it before first use; the certification itself stays out of the workspace (rule 3)]
- Statement of authority (§ 605.0302) and articles amendment, prepared now for filing under [ ].2(a)
